question: After exact-head live Android proof, should generated Kotlin serializers become the permanent Android gateway wire boundary?
rationale: The approach removes duplicate protocol ownership, but it changes a compatibility-sensitive runtime boundary whose long-term ownership and upgrade risk require Android-owner acceptance.

options.title: Accept generated boundary
options.body: Rebase, document the workflow, prove real Android interoperability, and merge if the generated serializers preserve existing wire behavior.

options.title: Generate catalogs only
options.body: Retain handwritten runtime frame serializers while generating method, event, capability, and command catalogs until broader device proof exists.

options.title: Pause the migration
options.body: Keep the current handwritten path and strengthen drift checks if the Android owner does not want generated runtime models.

recommendation.title: Accept generated boundary
recommendation.body: Rebase, document the workflow, prove real Android interoperability, and merge if the generated serializers preserve existing wire behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is the best available Android ownership route for a change to the app's central gateway serialization boundary.
